narrative: After the 2026-09-22 deployment, KPost's authentication is non-deterministic: roughly HALF of all successful logins mint a token that every authenticated endpoint then rejects. POST /v2/signupLogin/userLogin/ answers HTTP 200 with a well-formed, unexpired JWT (24h TTL, correct iat/exp), but when that token is presented to any authenticated resource endpoint the server answers HTTP 401 {"status":"FAILURE","statusCode":401,"message":"UNAUTHORIZED USER"}. The outcome is fixed per login: a token minted by one login is consistently accepted on every endpoint, and a token from the next login is consistently rejected on every endpoint, alternating almost exactly login-to-login. Measured 8 consecutive logins with the same account and payload: 4 produced a working token and 4 produced an unusable one (~50%). The token itself is valid (verified by decoding: signed, not expired), and the rejection is identical across unrelated endpoints (POST /v2/signupLogin/fetchUserDetails/ and POST /v2/profile/getMyProfile/ both return 401 for a 'bad' token and both succeed for a 'good' token), which rules out a per-endpoint bug. The signature — a valid token accepted or rejected wholesale depending only on which login produced it — points to login sessions/tokens not being shared across backend instances behind the load balancer (the login is served by one node and validated against another with no shared session store / no sticky routing). Impact: a real user has a ~50% chance that a fresh login leaves them unable to use any authenticated feature until they log in again; automated clients and the QA bench see every authenticated endpoint fail intermittently. This is a single systemic root cause, not a per-endpoint defect — it makes the entire authenticated API unreliable.
expected: Every token returned by a successful userLogin (HTTP 200) is accepted by all authenticated resource endpoints.
actual: ~50% of successful logins return a valid, unexpired token that every authenticated endpoint rejects with HTTP 401 'UNAUTHORIZED USER'; acceptance is fixed per token and alternates login-to-login.
repro:
Reproduced in 3/3 independent multi-login runs (the defect appears every time you attempt a handful of logins). Within each run, ~50% of individual logins yield a token the API rejects. Detailed steps:
1. POST /v2/signupLogin/userLogin/ with valid QA credentials -> HTTP 200 with accessToken (a valid, unexpired JWT).
2. Immediately POST /v2/signupLogin/fetchUserDetails/ {"kpostID":"<self>"} with Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>.
3. Observe the response is EITHER 200 (token accepted) OR 401 'UNAUTHORIZED USER' (token rejected) — fixed for that token.
4. Repeat login+call ~8 times. Measured result: 200,401,200,401,200,401,200,401 -> 4/8 (~50%) of logins yield a token rejected by every authenticated endpoint. Every multi-login run reproduces at least one rejected token.
5. Cross-check with a second endpoint (POST /v2/profile/getMyProfile/): a 'bad' token 401s there too and a 'good' token is accepted there too, confirming the fault is the token/session, not the endpoint.
curl:
# Mint a token
TOKEN=$(curl -s https://<KPOST_HOST>/v2/signupLogin/userLogin/ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"deviceType":"Web","deviceIdentity_primary":"<device>","deviceIdentity_secondary":"Desktop-Chrome","sessionID":"<uuid>","kpostID":"<QA_KPOST_ID>","loginRO":{"countryID":"1","password":"<QA_PASSWORD>","userType":"PERSONAL"},"logintime":0,"module":0}' | python -c 'import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)["accessToken"])')
# Present it to an authenticated endpoint (repeat a few fresh logins; ~half return 401)
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://<KPOST_HOST>/v2/signupLogin/fetchUserDetails/ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"kpostID":"<QA_KPOST_ID>"}'
note: Root-cause hypothesis: login session not replicated / not sticky across backend instances behind the LB (login on node A, token validated on node B). Fixing this unblocks the entire authenticated KPost API; until then automated runs must re-login until a token is accepted.
